explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1141 with the negative answer from [APSSV26b]: only finitely many n have n - k² prime for every k with gcd(n,k) = 1 and k² < n. The k = 0 case only matters for n = 1, which correctly fails. The test examples (968 fails, 1722 satisfies) calibrate the definition against the page and A214583.
